end.summary:
- Copying shapes on a dot or square grid was shown, including counting gaps along sides.
- Turning or moving a shape was practised; some answers were right, but this is not steady yet and needs checking next time.
- Tile patterns on a grid were practised once and are still building; the pattern was not continued.
- Myra mixed up counting dots with counting gaps on a dot grid, and this was not corrected later in the lesson.
end.parentNote: Myra practised copying shapes by counting the gaps between dots and identifying shapes after they were turned or moved. The gap-counting method worked during the copying questions, but they later returned to counting dots instead of gaps; this was not corrected by the end. Tile-pattern work is still building, so at home you can draw two dots, mark the one gap between them, and then continue a simple repeating tile pattern one step at a time.
